claimed.text: How the Grusch claims reached the public: Coulthart's NewsNation interview of 11 June 2023, the first on television, produced the dead pilots statement and the biologics claim that Grusch ratified under oath five weeks later. Kean and Blumenthal had reported his crash-retrieval claims on 5 June.

Michels's 11 January 2026 episode with the pseudonymous researcher UAP Gerb, its sole guest and source, frames the effort as "not one program" but "a layered, compartmentalized system that grew out of the Manhattan Project, the Atomic Energy Commission, and Cold War intelligence structures." It names MITRE, the Office of Global Access and the DOE NEST as components and says Dick Cheney is implicated.

American Alchemy's audience is large: the Jake Barber episode of 30 January 2025 has about 1.01 million views and the Gerb structural episode about 515,000. Michels also carried Shellenberger the day after the 2024 hearing and a three-episode Dylan Borland sequence in August 2026.

Coulthart carried Gerb's model into broadcast and endorsed it on air, "I think he's on the money", and on Reality Check Gerb alleged directed-energy attacks on people close to the programme, civilian aircraft downed by EMP weapons and a murder. The desk and the investigator share research: Gerb credits Reality Check's research producer Rob Jones with details on a new alleged gatekeeper.
NewsNation aired Barber's Skywatcher special in January 2025 and remains its main outlet; Barber's claims are unverified by official sources.

Knapp testified that Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with Lockheed Martin executives for unusual material held in California, "That material was not made here", named Lockheed and two alleged gatekeepers, and said EG&G's first Nevada manager told him a saucer and a live being had been recovered.
From the witness table Knapp said reprisals against witnesses are carried out by persons unknown, as Grusch, present in the room, knew; no member asked what he meant.

Knapp is credited with introducing Harry Reid to Robert Bigelow, and the board records that DIA's James Lacatski read Hunt for the Skinwalker, which Knapp co-wrote, before approaching Bigelow in 2007; Knapp also worked with Bigelow's NIDS.
Corbell has released leaked Navy footage associated with the USS Omaha and of apparently triangular objects.
Shellenberger's source alleges Immaculate Constellation is a parent unacknowledged programme consolidating UAP observations, created in 2017 in response to the Times story.

contested.text: The Pentagon said it has no record of Immaculate Constellation and Sean Kirkpatrick denied it existed. Jason Colavito concluded a 2025 claimant had mistaken wargame documents for secret revelations, though the board notes this does not account for the 12-page document of November 2024. Elizondo would neither confirm nor deny any programme by name.

Members of Congress call the release of Grusch's police records retaliation, while The Intercept says the records were publicly available law enforcement records obtained under a routine Virginia FOIA request, not leaked.

The Times did not publish the 2023 Grusch story; its authors placed it at The Debrief. The board records the change of venue and infers that it says something about institutional appetite; no record shows whether the Times was offered it.
Nothing from KLAS-TV's own account of its 1989 reporting is on the board, because the station's retrospectives were not reachable, and the air dates of the broadcasts rest on a secondary timeline.
Greenewald showed that the photograph circulated as Thomas Castello's leaked evidence is a frame from the 2000 film The 6th Day, and found no evidence Castello exists.

Klass did not attend the 2001 press conference, having been refused admission to a comparable event, so his account rests largely on Greer's releases and book; ABC's same-day report carried a sceptical comment from its space consultant.
The substrate is divided: third-party channels covered a public dispute between Gerb and Elizondo in August 2026, which Coulthart called a schism; no primary statement from either was retrieved.

The claim that no US paper of record has originated a legacy-programme disclosure since 2017 has at least one exception on the board: the Wall Street Journal reported in June 2025 that Air Force personnel had been briefed into a fictitious reverse-engineering programme called Yankee Blue.

lead.text: The disclosure record of 2017 to 2026 was carried less by newspapers than by a Las Vegas television station, one cable correspondent, an independent outlet, a newsletter and long-form podcasts. The New York Times broke AATIP in 2017, but the Grusch story, the Immaculate Constellation report and, on the board's reading, the most detailed structural reconstruction in circulation all went elsewhere first.

record.text: The New York Times story of 16 December 2017, bylined by Helene Cooper, Ralph Blumenthal and Leslie Kean, named the programme, the $22 million, Harry Reid and Robert Bigelow and identified Luis Elizondo as its director; Reid told the paper he was not embarrassed or sorry he got it going.

The Debrief was co-founded by Micah Hanks as editor-in-chief, Tim McMillan as executive director and MJ Banias as content director, and published the Kean and Blumenthal Grusch story after its authors placed it there rather than at the Times.

Hanks wrote The Debrief's 17 October 2024 report on Immaculate Constellation, framed as bombshell or disinformation, four weeks before the name reached Congress; the outlet has covered the AARO reports and the Disclosure Act's failures.

Immaculate Constellation reached the Congressional Record without a newsroom: Shellenberger reported it on Public and, testifying on 13 November 2024 as founder of Public, brought a 12-page document that Rep. Mace entered into the record.

Knapp testified on 9 September 2025 as 'UAP Journalist' and opened: "I am George Knapp, chief investigative reporter at KLAS-TV in Las Vegas." His KLAS I-Team had published AAWSAP contract documentation showing the DIA-funded study was executed in Las Vegas.

A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of 19 June 1990 confirms that Bob Lazar was the focal point of Knapp's award-winning KLAS-TV series, the only contemporaneous record the board holds that the 1989 broadcasts happened.

Jeremy Corbell directed Bob Lazar: Area 51 and Flying Saucers, 97 minutes, released between November and December 2018 and featuring Lazar and Knapp. At the 26 July 2023 hearing Rep. Burchett entered Corbell's report The UAP Puzzle and a statement by Knapp into the record, saying they were not witnesses.

McMillan obtained the police report of the 19 July 2017 FBI search of Lazar's business and showed it supported a homicide investigation into a thallium death in which Lazar is not recorded as a suspect.

Ken Klippenstein published in The Intercept, in August 2023, Loudoun County Sheriff's records of Grusch's 2014 and 2018 emergency custody episodes obtained under Virginia FOIA. In June 2019 The Intercept's Keith Kloor had reported no discernible evidence that Elizondo worked for, much less led, a government UFO programme.

The Intercept was established in 2014 as a non-profit funded by readers, taking no advertising and publishing audited financial statements. The Hill has run a series of UAP opinion pieces aimed at its congressional readership.

Greenewald's Black Vault has published well over two million pages since 1996, including the DD Form 1910 for the Navy videos and the Elizondo-Gough correspondence, and he found the FAA's Japan Air Lines 1628 file at the National Archives after the FAA twice told him it had been or would be destroyed.

ABC News reported the Disclosure Project's National Press Club event on 9 May 2001, organised by Steven Greer, at which about 20 former government workers came forward; Philip Klass recorded that 20 of the 69 witnesses in Greer's book spoke.
John Lear's own claim document is dated 29 December 1987 and was circulated on the ParaNet bulletin board in early 1988, about eighteen months before Lazar's KLAS appearance.

summary.text: The board measures the shift from the New York Times story of 16 December 2017, which it calls the last time a US paper of record originated a disclosure about the programme's existence; the same authors' 2023 Grusch story ran in The Debrief.

The substrate is small and identifiable: KLAS-TV in Las Vegas, where George Knapp has reported since 1981; NewsNation's single correspondent Ross Coulthart; Jesse Michels's American Alchemy and the Weaponized podcast; Michael Shellenberger's newsletter Public; and John Greenewald's FOIA archive, The Black Vault.
The board infers that long-form independent media lets claims be laid out at length and indexed, while its sponsorship, membership and tour revenue creates an incentive to escalate.
The same substrate holds its adversarial counterweight: The Intercept's reporting subtracted from the record, challenging Elizondo's AATIP role and publishing FOIA'd police records on Grusch.

title: Podcasts, broadcasters and independent media
